rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent immediate point is God's easing the burden of marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women, because people struggle to restrain desire for women.
rows.anchor: المقصد الظاهر بهذه الآية أنها في تخفيف الله تعالى ترك نكاح الإماء بإباحة ذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد وطاوس
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Tawus likewise understand human weakness here as weakness in resisting sexual desire for women.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال مجاهد وابن زيد وطاوس

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus says people are weaker in no matter than in matters concerning women.
rows.anchor: وقال طاوس: ليس يكون الإنسان في شيء أضعف منه في أمر النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond the immediate case, the verse expresses God's gracious easing in all matters and the ease of religion; human weakness is general because desire usually tempts people.
rows.anchor: ثم بعد هذا المقصد تخرج الآية في مخرج التفضل، لأنها تتناول كل ما خفف الله تعالى عن عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the majority reading, al-insan is passive-voice subject and da'ifan is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: والإنسان رفع على ما لم يسم فاعله، وضعيفا حال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid read the verb actively, with da'ifan still a circumstantial accusative; khalaqa may mean ja'ala, making it transitive to two objects and da'ifan the second.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد «وخلق الإنسان» على بناء الفعل للفاعل وضعيفا حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse honors and entrusts judgment to the Prophet, while correcting his judgment and reproaching him for initially accepting the report about Banu Ubayriq too quickly.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية تشريف للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتفويض إليه، وتقويم أيضا على الجادة في الحكم، وتأنيب ما على قبول ما رفع إليه في أمر بني أبيرق بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judging by what God showed means judging according to the law, through revelation and explicit text or reasoned judgment following revelation's way.
rows.anchor: بما أراك الله معناه: على قوانين الشرع، إما بوحي ونص، أو بنظر جار على سنن الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees that His prophets are protected from error in this matter.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمن الله تعالى لأنبيائه العصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that the warning and command to seek forgiveness arose from the Banu Ubayriq case.
rows.anchor: سببها باتفاق من المتأولين أمر بني أبيرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account, Bashir of the Ubayriq brothers was a hypocrite who mocked the Companions and falsely attributed others' poetry to them; one poem complained that men's poems were ascribed to Ibn al-Ubayriq.
rows.anchor: وكان بشير رجلا منافقا يهجو أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada reports that his uncle Rifa'a's food, two armors, and two swords were stolen from a storeroom; suspicion fell on the impoverished Banu Ubayriq after they lit a fire that night.
rows.anchor: فابتاع عمي رفاعة بن زيد حملا من دومك الشام فجعله في مشربة له

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that the Ubayriq brothers diverted suspicion to the upright Labid ibn Sahl, who confronted them with his sword; Qatada then told the Prophet, who initially rebuked him for accusing a righteous Muslim without proof.
rows.anchor: والله ما نرى صاحبكم إلا لبيد بن سهل، رجل منا له صلاح وإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account just related, the traitors are Banu Ubayriq, the innocent man framed is Labid ibn Sahl, and the plotting group is Usayr and his companions.
rows.anchor: فالخائنون بنو أبيرق، والبريء المرمي لبيد بن سهل، والطائفة التي همت: أسير وأصحابه

rows.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد من المتأولين
rows.claim: Qatada and other interpreters identify the culprit in the case as Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq, also called Tu'ayma.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وغير واحد من المتأولين: هذه القصة ونحوها إنما كان صاحبها طعمة بن أبيرق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Ta'ma denied stealing armor entrusted to him by a Jew, hid it in Abu Malil al-Ansari's house, and tried to frame Abu Malil when exposed; Abu Malil was innocent.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: القصة في طعمة بن أبيرق لكن بأن استودعه يهودي درعا فجحده إياها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Ta'ma stole armor from a storeroom and accused a Jew named Zayd ibn al-Samin of the theft.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: سرق طعمة بن أبيرق درعا من مشربة ورمى بسرقتها رجلا من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared substance is that Ta'ma's people petitioned the Prophet to defend him and withdraw the charge, although some knew he had stolen; believing members sinned, hypocrites acted deliberately, and God protected His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وجملة هذا يستدير على أن قوم طعمة أتوا النبي وكلموه في أن يذب عن طعمة ويرفع الدعوى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Ta'ima later apostatized and fled to Mecca; after Sulafa received Hassan ibn Thabit's poem about him, she expelled him and threw out his belongings.
rows.anchor: وطعيمة بن أبيرق صرح بعد ذلك بالارتداد وهرب إلى مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports give different endings for Ta'ma: Hajjaj ibn Allat expelled him after a theft, a collapsing wall killed him while burgling, or Arabs killed him after he robbed them.
rows.anchor: فروي: أنه نزل على الحجاج بن علاط وسرقه فطرده، وروي أنه نقب حائط بيت ليسرقه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes the command to seek forgiveness as requiring the Prophet to repent for his sin in arguing on behalf of the traitors.
rows.anchor: ذهب الطبري إلى أن المعنى استغفر الله من ذنبك في خصامك للخائنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that ascribing a sin to the Prophet: he defended the apparent case while believing them innocent; the command instead means asking forgiveness for sinful community members and false litigants, while hearing both sides, judging on the evidence presented, and seeking forgiveness for the sinner.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بذنب، لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دافع عن الظاهر، وهو يعتقد براءتهم

words: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلْ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against arguing for those who betray themselves is general, includes the people in this case, and reproaches them.
rows.anchor: لفظ عام يندرج طيه أصحاب النازلة ويتقرر به توبيخهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording conveys lenience and forbearance, leaving a single lapse or inadvertent betrayal outside the description of a habitual intentional traitor.
rows.anchor: رفق وإبقاء، فإن الخوان: هو الذي تتكرر منه الخيانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwan describes repeated betrayal, while athim describes someone who intends it; this excludes a one-time lapse or betrayal without intent, such as through inattention.
rows.anchor: فإن الخوان: هو الذي تتكرر منه الخيانة، والأثيم: هو الذي يقصدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Betraying oneself means incurring the sin and punishment that return upon oneself in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: واختيان الأنفس: هو بما يعود عليها من الإثم والعقوبة في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasb means earning; ithm is the consequence of disobedience and the resulting ascription of punishment.
rows.anchor: «والإثم» الحكم اللاحق عن المعصية، ونسبة المرء إلى العقوبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who earns sin brings ruin and harm upon himself.
rows.anchor: أي إياها يردي وبها يحل المكروه

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some take khati'a and ithm as synonyms, repeated for verbal variation.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض الناس إلى أنهما لفظان بمعنى كرر لاختلاف اللفظ

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes the terms: khati'a can be deliberate or inadvertent, whereas ithm is only deliberate.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: إنما فرق بين «الخطيئة والإثم» أن الخطيئة تكون عن عمد وعن غير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's general wording also reproaches those involved in the earlier case; its innocent victim is variously identified as Labid ibn Sahl, Zayd ibn al-Samin, or Abu Malil al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية لفظها عام، ويندرج تحت ذلك العموم وتوبيخه أهل النازلة المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ihtamala is a metaphor: sins are burdens and weights that a person carries.
rows.anchor: تشبيه، إذ الذنوب ثقل ووزر، فهي كالمحمولات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buhtan is a lie against an innocent person; the Prophet distinguishes truthful but disliked speech about a brother as backbiting from false speech as slander.
rows.anchor: وبهتانا معناه: كذبا على البريء، ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا قلت في أخيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false accuser commits two offenses: the underlying sin and the additional offense of falsely accusing an innocent person.
rows.anchor: فرمي البريء بهت له ونفس الخطيئة والإثم إثم مبين، ومعصية هذا الرامي معصيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hammat means that the group would make misleading the Prophet its consuming purpose until it carried it out.
rows.anchor: لهمت معناه: لجعلته همها وشغلها حتى تنفذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is general beyond this case: without God's protection, people would set themselves to mislead the Prophet as these partisans did, but protection defeats their plots and leaves misguidance with them.
rows.anchor: وإلا فأهل التعصب لبني أبيرق قد وقع همهم وثبت، وإنما المعنى: ولولا عصمة الله لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through the recited Book and wisdom, God taught the Prophet what he had not known; the remainder of the verse is self-explanatory.
rows.anchor: وبهذين علمه ما لم يكن يعلم، وباقي الآية بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the recited revelation; wisdom includes teachings given to the Prophet and a native, cultivated faculty for judging among people, through which he was taught what he did not know and does not speak from whim.
rows.anchor: والحكمة التي بعضها خوطب به وبعضها جعلت له سجية ملكها، وقريحة يعمل عنها، وينظر بين الناس بها، لا ينطق عن الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atlu means narrate and make them hear; naba' means a report.
rows.anchor: اتل معناه اسرد وأسمعهم إياه، وهذه من علوم الكتب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is knowledge from earlier scriptures, inaccessible to Muhammad except by revelation, so it is evidence of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: لا تعلق لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بها إلا من طريق الوحي، فهو من دلائل نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun most likely addresses the Children of Israel: the preceding argument addresses them, and the obscure story was known from their scriptures, making its telling a proof against them.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليهم ظاهر أمره أنه يراد به بنو إسرائيل لوجهين: أحدهما أن المحاورة فيما تقدم

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes identify the two sons as Cain and Abel, biological sons of Adam.
rows.anchor: و «ابنا آدم» هما في قول جمهور المفسرين لصلبه. وهما قابيل وهابيل

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says they were not Adam's biological sons and that sacrifices occurred only among the Israelites; Ibn Atiyya calls this mistaken because Israelites would not be ignorant of burial until the crow taught them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري «ابنا آدم» ليسا لصلبه ولم تكن القرابين إلا في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the brothers made their offerings as voluntary devotion.
rows.anchor: وروي أن تقريبهما للقربان إنما كان تحنثا وتطوعا

words: فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلْءَاخَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain, a farmer, offered his worst produce, while Abel, a shepherd, offered his best ram; their custom was to pray after offering, and a descending fire signaled acceptance, taking Abel's ram and leaving Cain's crop.
rows.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع فعمد إلى أرذل ما عنده وأدناه فقربه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others say Abel's ram grazed in Paradise until it was sent down to Abraham as the ransom for his son.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وغيره: فكان ذلك الكبش يرتع في الجنة حتى أهبط إلى إبراهيم

rows.speaker: سائقو هذا القصص
rows.claim: Storytellers say Cain envied Abel and resented that people regarded Abel as better; Cain was Adam's eldest son.
rows.anchor: فحسد قابيل هابيل وقال له: أتمشي على الأرض يراك الناس أفضل مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam travelled to Mecca to see the Ka'ba, left Cain overseeing his children, and the episode occurred during his absence.
rows.anchor: وروي أن «آدم» سافر إلى مكة ليرى الكعبة وترك قابيل وصيا على بنيه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: A report says Eve bore a boy and girl in each pregnancy; Adam arranged cross-twin marriages, but Cain wanted his own attractive twin sister, disobeyed Adam, and the brothers agreed to offer sacrifices.
rows.anchor: وروت جماعة من المفسرين منهم ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Adam witnessed the offerings; Abel's acceptance meant Cain had to accept the other marriage match, after which Cain threatened him.
rows.anchor: وروي أن آدم حضر ذلك فتقبل قربان هابيل ووجب أن يأخذ أخت قابيل، فحينئذ قال له لأقتلنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel's reply has an omitted preceding question: why kill me when I am guiltless of your rejected offering? I feared God and followed truth; God accepts only the Godfearing.
rows.anchor: وقول هابيل: إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين كلام قبله محذوف تقديره ولم تقتلني وأنا لم أجن شيئا

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna agree that taqwa here means avoiding shirk: a monotheist whose sincere works are genuine has them accepted; avoiding both shirk and sins brings the highest degree of acceptance and assured mercy, known through God's reports rather than rational obligation upon Him.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق: وإجماع أهل السنة في معنى هذه الألفاظ أنها اتقاء الشرك، فمن اتقاه وهو موحد

rows.speaker: عدي بن ثابت وغيره
rows.claim: Adi ibn Thabit and others say the offering of this community's Godfearing people is prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال عدي بن ثابت وغيره: قربان متقي هذه الأمة الصلاة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says people at that time were commanded neither to draw a sword nor to resist someone who sought to kill them.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد: كان الفرض عليهم حينئذ أن لا يسل أحد سيفا وأن لا يمتنع من أريد قتله

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr and the majority say Abel was stronger than Cain but refrained scrupulously.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس: كان هابيل أشد قوة من قابيل، ولكنه تحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the strength-and-scruple view: Abel's restraint suggests Cain was a sinner rather than an unbeliever, since scruple would make no sense otherwise; the scrupulous person accepts oppression for afterlife reward, as Uthman did.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رضي الله عنه: وهذا هو الأظهر. ومن هنا يقوى أن قابيل إنما هو عاص لا كافر

words: إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel's stated wish is not desire or pleasure in evil; it is choosing between two evils, as Arabs say that even in evil there is a choice: if killed, he chooses to be wronged and vindicated by God in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ليست هذه بإرادة محبة وشهوة، وإنما هو تخير في شرين، كما تقول العرب في الشر خيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabu'u means to depart bearing a burden.
rows.anchor: وتبوء معناه تمضي متحملا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the two sins as Abel's murder plus Cain's other sins that caused his offering to be rejected.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه: بإثم قتلي وسائر آثامك التي أوجبت أن لا يتقبل منك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes them as Abel's murder and Cain's sinful hostility and intention to kill, even if he never carried it out.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى: بإثم قتلي وإثمك في العداء علي إذ هو في العداء وإرادة القتل آثم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third interpretation is Abel's sin had he fought and killed Cain, together with Cain's sin in fighting and killing Abel; Ibn Atiyya prefers this sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى: بإثمي إن لو قاتلتك وقتلتك وإثم نفسك في قتالي وقتلي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when two Muslims meet with swords, both killer and killed are in Hell because the killed person was eager to kill his opponent; Ibn Atiyya uses this to support the third interpretation.
rows.anchor: إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار، قيل يا رسول الله هذا القاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the wrongdoer bears Abel's sins by way of compensation for his injustice, in addition to his own sin in killing him.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى: بإثمي الذي يختص لي فيما فرط لي أي يؤخذ من سيئاتي فيطرح عليك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that at resurrection an oppressor's good deeds are transferred to the oppressed; if none remain, the oppressed person's sins are put on the oppressor, supporting the compensatory interpretation.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالظالم والمظلوم يوم القيامة فيؤخذ من حسنات الظالم فيزاد في حسنات المظلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement may be spoken by Abel to his brother or may be God's report to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وذلك جزاء الظالمين يحتمل أن يكون من قول هابيل لأخيه، ويحتمل أن يكون إخبارا من الله

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority reading faṭawwaʿat portrays the rebellious, evil-commanding soul as making intrinsically difficult murder seem compliant and easy until Cain commits it.
rows.anchor: قراءة الجمهور فطوعت والمعنى أن القتل في ذاته مستصعب عظيم على النفوس

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن والجراح والحسن بن عمران وأبو واقد
rows.claim: These readers have faṭāwaʿat: Cain's hatred and envy made killing beckon while his soul resisted, until the soul yielded to the act.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن والجراح والحسن بن عمران وأبو واقد «فطاوعت» والمعنى كأن القتل يدعو إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Cain waited for an opportunity, found Abel asleep among his sheep, and smashed his head with a stone.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه التمس الغرة في قتله حتى وجده نائما في غنمه فشدخ رأسه بحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Cain did not know how to kill until Iblis showed him by smashing a bird or other animal's head between two stones.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه جهل كيف يقتله فجاء إبليس بطائر أو حيوان غيره فجعل يشدخ رأسه بين حجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam asked where Abel was; Cain denied knowing, and Adam cursed the ground for drinking Abel's blood, after which earth did not drink blood.
rows.anchor: والله إن دمه ليناديني من الأرض، اللهم العن أرضا شربت دم هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Adam did not smile for a hundred years until an angel greeted him and explained that bayyaka meant making him laugh.
rows.anchor: فقال آدم: ما بياك؟ قال أضحكك

rows.speaker: آدم عليه السلام
rows.claim: A poem attributed to Adam laments that the land and its people changed, the earth became dusty and ugly, tastes and colors changed, and cheerful beautiful faces became scarce.
rows.anchor: تغيرت البلاد ومن عليها ... فوجه الأرض مغبر قبيح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that the killer's leg was attached to his thigh until Judgment Day, his face turned toward the sun, with enclosures of fire and winter snow; the author says, if authentic, this is among his losses.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أنه قال علقت إحدى رجلي القاتل بساقها إلى فخذها من يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the first killer shares the Hell-dwellers' punishment equally, bearing half their torment.
rows.anchor: ومن خسرانه ما روي عن عبد الله بن عمرو أنه قال إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author calls this authentic: every soul unjustly killed gives the first son of Adam a share of its guilt because he first instituted murder.
rows.anchor: «ما قتلت نفس ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول كفل منها، وذلك أنه أول من سن القتل»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asbaha can describe all of someone's time, with part of a period standing for the whole; morning is singled out as the day's beginning and the start of activity and vigor.
rows.anchor: فأصبح عبارة عن جميع أوقاته أقيم بعض الزمن مقام كله، وخص الصباح بذلك لأنه بدء النهار

rows.speaker: الربيع بن ضبع
rows.claim: The poet al-Rabi ibn Dab' illustrates this Arabic use of asbaha with a line beginning, “I have come to morning not bearing arms.”
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الربيع بن ضبع: أصبحت لا أحمل السلاح البيت

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas likewise uses asbaha for a continuing state, saying that the sons of Asad then began to punish him for Islam.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول سعد بن أبي وقاص، ثم أصبحت بنو أسد تعزرني على الإسلام

words: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say Cain carried Abel in a sack on his neck for a hundred years, or one year; another says that the next day he sought to conceal his brother but did not know how.
rows.anchor: روي في معناه أن قابيل جعل أخاه في جراب ومشى به يحمله في عنقه مائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report has God send a living crow to a dead crow, where it scratches and throws soil over the corpse; another has two crows fight until one kills the other and buries it; another says one crow buried Abel.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله غرابا حيا إلى غراب ميت فجعل يبحث في الأرض ويلقي التراب على الغراب الميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent sense makes Abel the first human to die, explaining why the burial practice was unknown; al-Tabari transmits this from Ibn Ishaq on the authority of a scholar of the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذه الآية أن هابيل هو أول ميت من بني آدم، ولذلك جهلت سنة المواراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yabhathu means searching through soil with the beak and stirring it; the name of Surat Bara'a, al-Buhuth, reflects its exposure of hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ويبحث معناه يفتش التراب بمنقاره ويثيره، ومن هذا سميت سورة براءة البحوث لأنها فتشت عن المنافقين

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet's line uses bahathuni for people investigating someone; a proverb warns against being like one searching for an awl.
rows.anchor: إن الناس غطوني تغطيت عنهم ... وإن بحثوني كان فيهم مباحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “his brother” may refer to Cain, with Abel as his brother, or to the searching crow, with the dead crow as its brother; the first is the more famous interpretation.
rows.anchor: والضمير في قوله: سوأة أخيه يحتمل أن يعود على قابيل ويراد بالأخ هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saw'a means the nakedness; it is singled out though the whole body is buried because covering it is especially important, or it may denote the whole distressing sight, attributed to the victim because the event befell him, while disgrace belongs to the killer.
rows.anchor: والسوأة العورة، وخصت بالذكر مع أن المراد مواراة جميع الجسد للاهتمام بها

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read fa-uwariya with the ya in the subjunctive, with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «فأواري» بنصب الياء

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف والفياض بن غزوان
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif and al-Fayyad ibn Ghazwan read fa-uwari with a quiescent ya, a language variant arising from consecutive vowel movements.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف والفياض بن غزوان «فأواري» بسكون الياء، وهي لغة لتوالي الحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crow's example taught Cain how to bury his brother; he realized human inadequacy and ignorance and despised himself, which led to regret.
rows.anchor: ولما رأى قابيل فعل الغراب تنبه على ما يجب أن يصنع بأخيه، ورأى قصور نفسه وجهل البشر بالأمور

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read ya waylata; its original form is ya waylati, but some Arabs replace final ya with alif and open the preceding ya, as in ya ghulama, and some pause with ha' of pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «يا ويلتى» والأصل «يا ويلتي» لكن من العرب من يبدل من الياء ألفا

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri is also reported reading ya waylata.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «يا ويلتى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry means “come, misfortune, this is your time”; Arabic similarly calls out abstract meanings such as “O grief” and “O wonder.”
rows.anchor: ونداء الويلة هو على معنى احضري فهذا أوانك، وهذا هو الباب في قوله يا حسرة [يس: 30]

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read aʿajiztu with fatḥa on the jim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «أعجزت» بفتح الجيم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن والفياض وطلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, Hasan, al-Fayyad, and Talha ibn Sulayman read the jim with kasra, a recognized dialect variant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والحسن والفياض وطلحة بن سليمان «أعجزت» بكسر الجيم، وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain buried his brother and regretted disobeying God, but regret came too late to help him.
rows.anchor: ثم إن قابيل وارى أخاه وندم على ما كان منه من معصية الله في قتله حيث لا ينفعه الندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ whether Cain was an unbeliever or a sinner; Ibn Atiyya says the apparent view is that he was a sinner.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء في قابيل هل هو من الكفار أو من العصاة، والظاهر أنه من العصاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report presents Adam's two sons as an example for the community: take the better one as a model and leave the worse.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال «إن الله ضرب لكم ابني آدم مثلا فخذوا من خيرهما ودعوا الشر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address continues the command not to take Jews and Christians as allies in 5:51; innama restricts the guardianship named here, and wali is a generic noun.
rows.anchor: الخطاب بقوله: إنما وليكم الله الآية للقوم الذين قيل لهم لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء [المائدة: 51]

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads inna-mawlākum Allah, using mawlākum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «إنما موليكم الله»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are those truly faithful rather than hypocrites, who establish obligatory prayer with all its conditions.
rows.anchor: أي ومن آمن من الناس حقيقة لا نفاقا وهم الذين يقيمون الصلاة المفروضة بجميع شروطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat here broadly includes obligatory alms, voluntary charity, and every good deed, which increases good works and purifies a person from sin; believers give according to their capacity.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا لفظ عام للزكاة المفروضة وللتطوع بالصدقة ولكل أفعال البر، إذ هي تنمية للحسنات

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads with an additional conjunction: amanu wa-alladhina yuqimuna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «آمنوا والذين يقيمون» بواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause wa-hum raki'un is coordinated with the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وهم راكعون جملة معطوفة على جملة

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority understand this as describing abundant prayer: rukūʿ is singled out as a major pillar and humble posture standing for the whole prayer, as “the bowing and prostrating” does in 2:125.
rows.anchor: وخص الركوع بالذكر لكونه من أعظم أركان الصلاة، وهو هيئة تواضع فعبر به عن جميع الصلاة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerns believers generally, but happened to coincide with Ali ibn Abi Talib giving his ring to a beggar while bowing in the mosque.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: هذه الآية في جمع المؤمنين ولكن عليا بن أبي طالب مر به سائل وهو راكع في المسجد فأعطاه خاتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet, after the verse was revealed, asked a beggar whether anyone had given him anything; the beggar described a silver ring given by a praying man while bowing, and the Prophet identified Ali and recited the verse.
rows.anchor: وروي في ذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من بيته وقد نزلت عليه الآية فوجد مسكينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With al-kuffar genitive, the phrase includes disbelievers among those who ridicule the believers' religion; Qur'an 15:95 establishes mockery by disbelievers, 5:57 by People of the Book, and 2:14 by hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ويدخل «الكفار» على قراءة الخفض فيمن اتخذ دين المؤمنين هزؤا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites 15:95 for the disbelievers' mockery and 2:14 for hypocrites telling their devils, “we are only mocking.”
rows.anchor: وثبت استهزاء أهل الكتاب في لفظ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With al-kuffar accusative, the word attaches to the verb la tattakhidhu, so this phrase no longer indicates their mockery.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ «الكفار» بالنصب حمل على الفعل الذي هو لا تتخذوا، ويخرج الكفار من أن يتضمن لفظ هذه الآية استهزاءهم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay ibn Ka'b adds min before al-kuffar, supporting the genitive reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب «ومن الكفار» بزيادة «من» فهذه تؤيد قراءة الخفض

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud's reading adds “min those who associated” after “from before you,” also supporting the genitive reading.
rows.anchor: وكذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود «من قبلكم من الذي أشركوا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuffar commonly denotes idol-worshipping polytheists, regarded as the furthest in disbelief; scripture distinguishes them from People of the Book and hypocrites, who believe in God and some prophets or profess belief only verbally.
rows.anchor: وفرقت الآية بين الكفار وبين الذين أوتوا الكتاب من حيث الغلب في اسم الكفار أن يقع على المشركين بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate command “strive against the disbelievers and hypocrites” in 9:73 illustrates that scripture distinguishes these groups even though both are classed as unbelievers, since idolaters disbelieve in every respect.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى: جاهد الكفار والمنافقين [التوبة: 73] ففرق بينهم إرادة البيان والجمع كفار وكان هذا لأن عباد الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing exhortation commands reverence for God and challenges the audience to be genuine believers.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر تعالى بتقواه ونبه النفوس بقوله: إن كنتم مؤمنين أي حق مؤمنين
